sub_unit_name: Rubbers: Natural rubber and its vulcanization

content.title: Rubbers
content.description: Rubbers are natural or synthetic elastomeric polymers that can undergo large elastic deformation and regain their original shape when the applied force is removed.

content.content: Rubber is an important engineering material due to its excellent elasticity, flexibility, shock absorption, and resistance to wear. The most common natural rubber is obtained from the latex of the rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis).

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Rubbers are widely used in tyres, tubes, conveyor belts, seals, gaskets, hoses, footwear, and vibration dampers because of their elasticity and durability.

Natural rubber is obtained from the latex of the Hevea brasiliensis tree. Chemically, it is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, formed by the polymerization of isoprene molecules. It possesses high elasticity but has poor resistance to heat, oils, and chemicals.

items.question: High Elasticity
items.answer: Returns to its original shape after deformation.

items.question: Good Tensile Strength
items.answer: Can withstand considerable stretching before breaking.

items.question: Poor Heat Resistance
items.answer: Becomes soft at high temperatures and brittle at low temperatures.

items.question: Low Chemical Resistance
items.answer: Attacked by oils, solvents, oxygen, and ozone.

items.question: Good Electrical Insulation
items.answer: Acts as a good insulator under normal conditions.

content.content: Natural rubber has several drawbacks such as low mechanical strength, stickiness at high temperatures, brittleness at low temperatures, and poor resistance to chemicals. These disadvantages are overcome by the process of vulcanization.

Vulcanization is the process of heating natural rubber with about 3–5% sulfur (for soft rubber) at approximately 100–140°C. Sulfur forms cross-links between adjacent polymer chains, improving the physical and mechanical properties of rubber.

rows: Better resistance to oils and solvents

content.content: Vulcanized rubber is extensively used in automobile tyres, conveyor belts, electrical insulation, shoe soles, industrial rollers, hoses, gaskets, seals, shock absorbers, and vibration control components.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Remember the definition of vulcanization, the role of sulfur, the improvements in properties after vulcanization, and the comparison between natural and vulcanized rubber.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Natural rubber is obtained from Hevea brasiliensis latex.
Natural rubber has good elasticity but poor heat and chemical resistance.
Vulcanization is carried out by heating rubber with sulfur.
Sulfur forms cross-links between polymer chains.
Vulcanized rubber has higher strength, elasticity, and durability.
Vulcanized rubber is widely used in tyres, belts, hoses, and industrial products.
